Find \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\) if \(y = \dfrac{1}{x^2}\).
solution: Write \(y = x^{-2}\). Then \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -2x^{-3} = -\dfrac{2}{x^3}\). Matches option B.

optB: The slope of the tangent to the curve

solution: The derivative at a point gives the slope of the tangent to the curve at that point. Matches option B.

solution: The derivative of any constant is \(0\). Matches option C.

stem: If the displacement of an object is constant over time \((x = c)\), its velocity is:
solution: \(v = \dfrac{dx}{dt} = \dfrac{d}{dt}(c) = 0\). A constant displacement means zero velocity. Matches option C.

stem: According to the power rule, \(\dfrac{d}{dx}(x^n)\) is:
solution: By the power rule, \(\dfrac{d}{dx}(x^n) = n\,x^{n-1}\). Matches option B.

The displacement of a particle moving in a straight line is \(s = 2t^3 - 9t^2 + 12t\). At what time(s) does the particle come to rest momentarily?
solution: Velocity \(v = \dfrac{ds}{dt} = 6t^2 - 18t + 12 = 6(t-1)(t-2)\). Setting \(v = 0\) gives \(t = 1\,\text{s}\) and \(t = 2\,\text{s}\). Matches option A.

stem: Geometrically, the definite integral \(\int_a^b f(x)\,dx\) represents:
optA: The slope of the curve between \(a\) and \(b\)
optB: The area under the curve \(f(x)\) from \(x = a\) to \(x = b\)
optC: The maximum value of the function
solution: The definite integral \(\int_a^b f(x)\,dx\) gives the area under the curve \(f(x)\) between \(x = a\) and \(x = b\). Matches option B.

stem: If the velocity of an object is constant \((v = u)\), its displacement after time \(t\) can be found by evaluating \(\int_0^t u\,dt\). This equals:
solution: \(\int_0^t u\,dt = u\,[t']_0^t = ut\). Matches option B.
